instruction: Install the unpacked Chrome extension located in the 'helloExtension' folder on my Desktop.

parameters.command: echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt-get update -y && echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt-get install unzip -y && unzip /home/user/Desktop/helloExtension.zip -d /home/user/Desktop/ && rm /home/user/Desktop/helloExtension.zip

metadata.explanation: Variation 1: Changes evaluation from checking path to checking extension name. Uses existing getter get_find_installed_extension_name which returns list of extension names from Chrome Preferences. Custom metric checks if 'Hello Extensions' (from manifest.json) is in the installed extensions list.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter logic correctly extracts extension names from Chrome Preferences file (extensions.settings.{id}.manifest.name)
Metric function correctly handles expected parameter - uses expected.get('expected_name') which is correct for type='rule'
Verification logic is semantically sound: checks if expected extension name is in list of installed extensions
Data flow is correct: getter returns list of strings → metric checks if expected name is in list → returns 1.0 or 0.0
Evaluator properly verifies the instruction requirement: confirms the unpacked extension was successfully added to Chrome
Minor uncertainty: expected_name 'Hello Extensions' should match the actual name in manifest.json, but cannot verify without seeing the actual manifest file
